The criterion specifically requires proving that every paragraph exists twice in delivered markup—one normal-flow copy and one copy inside an inert scroll-driven layer. Visible text and scrolling alone cannot distinguish two overlaid copies from one copy, and the collected browser evidence did not directly inspect paragraph nodes or their containers. Therefore the observations do not defensibly settle the criterion.

Direct runtime animation evidence confirms the required persistent animated speckle on the letter. Its effect ordering relative to the later opacity animations supports the specified layer order beneath the darkening panels, while the simultaneously visible and readable letter content shows the overlay does not obscure the writing.

The shop presents exactly five products in one stable, non-price and non-name order. No search, filter, or sort mechanism appears on the catalogue page in either desktop or mobile navigation, so the fixed editorial arrangement requirement is met.

Direct inspection of two shop product pages shows a clearly labelled Specifications section organized into consistent two-column label/value rows. Numeric figures occupy the value column rather than being embedded in prose or ragged standalone text, satisfying the required tabular alignment.

The observations establish that the cart presents in-place quantity controls, but they do not settle the full composite criterion. The required server-rejection behavior could not be triggered because the over-stock increment was prevented client-side, and no pending-totals state or rejection/reversion message was directly observed. Therefore a defensible yes/no result is not available.
The discontinued Monitor Mount directly states both that it is no longer sold and the exact date through which support continues, satisfying R6.

The browser-name explanation and Arranger path are present, but the criterion requires the explanation to appear in place of any connect control. A nonfunctional disabled Connect control is still rendered, which the evaluation rule explicitly classifies as a failure.

The cart explicitly labels both delivery and tax as estimates and places a note beneath the totals stating that the exact amount will be shown once the destination is known. Validation and continuation through the address flow confirm the timing required by R8.

The criterion specifically concerns whether an ended warranty is displayed neutrally rather than as a warning/error. All directly observed warranties were future-dated, leaving no expired instance from which to determine the treatment.

The requirement applies conjunctively to the shop, cart, account, and download surfaces. Although cart, account, and downloads are dense and unornamented, the shop’s exceptionally tall 403–437px product tiles for only a few lines of text create generous merchandising space and fail the tightly set requirement. Because one required surface violates the rule, the criterion is not satisfied.

Go to your cart,” and /cart then showed the line item, quantity controls, subtotal, delivery, tax, total, protection option, and checkout link in a compact information-oriented layout.

The authenticated /account surface presented cameras, warranties, recent orders, and software release information as compact text/table data; inspected elements had no background image and zero margins.

The /downloads surface presented download metadata, hashes, firmware links, release notes, improvements, fixes, and known issues as dense text. Its primary download control measured 42px high with 8px 16px padding and no background image; the release-link styling also had no background image and zero padding/margin.
verdicts.rationale: The requirement applies conjunctively to the shop, cart, account, and download surfaces. Although cart, account, and downloads are dense and unornamented, the shop’s exceptionally tall 403–437px product tiles for only a few lines of text create generous merchandising space and fail the tightly set requirement. Because one required surface violates the rule, the criterion is not satisfied.

evidence: At 1440×900 on /shop, the persistent navigation/account rail was visible as separate controls aligned at x=20 with width=203: Shop y=96, Overview y=288, Orders y=332, Cameras y=376, and Sign out y=820; shop content began separately at x=253.

After resizing to 390×844 and refreshing the snapshot on /shop, the individual rail controls were absent and replaced by one button labeled “Sections” at x=212, y=20, size 89×40. Main product content began below it (first product x=21, y=227, width=348), with no observed horizontal clipping.

Activating “Sections” on narrow /shop exposed the same rail destinations (Shop, Downloads, Firmware installer, Overview, Orders, Cameras, Sign out), establishing that the single control is the rail replacement rather than unrelated navigation.
On narrow /cart, the same single “Sections” control appeared at x=212, y=20, size 89×40; activating it exposed the same complete navigation/account set.
From the narrow cart menu, selecting Overview navigated toward the account area, showing the replacement control provides access across shop, cart, and account navigation.
verdicts.rationale: Direct wide-versus-phone geometry establishes that the persistent 203px left rail collapses into exactly one top control on narrow layouts. Interaction verifies that this control expands to the original rail destinations, and its presence was directly observed on both shop and cart; the account destination was accessible through that same responsive navigation.

evidence: On route `/`, the interactive-element inventory contains three links: `Skip to the letter`, the `vela` wordmark, and `Shop`. Thus there is a navigation element beyond the wordmark and Shop/footer link.
The extra `Skip to the letter` link has `href="#letter"`; its geometry is initially off-screen at y=-100, but it is present and keyboard-accessible.

After pressing Tab, focus moved to `Skip to the letter`; it became visible at x=20, y=8 with a solid 2px focus outline. Pressing Enter navigated to `/#letter` and focused `<main id="letter">`, directly confirming the link's navigation behavior.
The full letter text showed no separate form-field or displayed product-price control; the observed defect is specifically the additional skip-navigation element.
verdicts.rationale: The criterion says any navigation element other than the wordmark and footer row is a defect. The letter page directly exposes a functional, keyboard-accessible `Skip to the letter` navigation link in addition to the `vela` wordmark and footer Shop link, so the negative anti-pattern is observed.
